Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal I$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf
of finite type on a scheme $X$
([[def-quasi-coherent-ideal-sheaf]]), let
$\pi\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\to X$ be the blowup of
[[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]] with center $Z=V(\mathcal I)$, and let
$W\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme
([[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]). Write
$\mathcal J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_W$ for the inverse image ideal of
$\mathcal I$ in $W$; it is a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf of finite type, and
it cuts out the scheme-theoretic intersection $W\cap Z$. Then the strict
transform $W'$ of $W$ ([[def-strict-transform-closed-subscheme]]), the
scheme-theoretic closure of $\pi^{-1}(W\smallsetminus Z)$ in
$W\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$, is canonically isomorphic over
$W$ to the blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}W$; equivalently, $W'$ is
the blowup of $W$ along the closed subscheme $W\cap Z$. On the standard
affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with
$\mathcal I=(f_0,\dots,f_r)$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$, the chart
$\operatorname{Spec}A[\mathcal I/f_i]$ of the blowup meets $W'$ in
$\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(A[\mathcal I/f_i]\big/\bigl(KA[\mathcal I/f_i]:f_i^\infty\bigr)\Bigr)$:
$W'$ is cut out by the saturation of the pullback ideal of $W$ by the
exceptional equation. Moreover the strict transform of a finite scheme-theoretic
union is the union of the strict transforms; in particular a finite
union of components is transformed componentwise, and $W'$ is not a single dominant component.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a regular surface
proper over $k$ with an ample invertible sheaf, let $C\subseteq S$ be a
reduced curve (an effective Cartier divisor), let $p$ be a closed point of
$S$ with residue degree $r=[\kappa(p):k]$ and let
$m=\operatorname{mult}_p(C)\ge1$ be the multiplicity of a local equation of
$C$ at $p$ ([[def-multiplicity-hypersurface-point]]). Let
$\pi\colon S'\to S$ be the blowup of $p$ with exceptional curve $E$ and let
$C'$ be the strict transform of $C$. Then
$\pi^*C=C'+mE$ as effective Cartier divisors on $S'$, and writing
$\chi_k(\mathcal O_X):=\chi_k(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for the Euler characteristic
of the structure sheaf ([[def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf]]), one has
$$\chi_k(\mathcal O_{C'})=\chi_k(\mathcal O_C)+r\binom{m}{2}.$$
Consequently, for the normalization defect
$\delta_k$ of [[def-normalization-defect-of-reduced-curve]],
$$\delta_k(C')=\delta_k(C)-r\binom{m}{2}.$$
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a regular surface
proper over $k$ with an ample invertible sheaf, let $C\subseteq S$ be a
reduced curve (an effective Cartier divisor), let $p$ be a closed point of
$S$ with residue degree $r=[\kappa(p):k]$ and let
$m=\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m_p}(f)\ge1$ be the order of a local
equation $f$ of $C$ in $\mathcal O_{S,p}$, namely
$f\in\mathfrak m_p^m\setminus\mathfrak m_p^{m+1}$. This is the intrinsic
multiplicity, agreeing with [[def-multiplicity-hypersurface-point]] in its
affine rational-point setting. Let
$\pi\colon S'\to S$ be the blowup of $p$ with exceptional curve $E$ and let
$C'$ be the strict transform of $C$. Then
$\pi^*C=C'+mE$ as effective Cartier divisors on $S'$, and writing
$\chi_k(\mathcal O_X):=\chi_k(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for the Euler characteristic
of the structure sheaf ([[def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf]]), one has
$$\chi_k(\mathcal O_{C'})=\chi_k(\mathcal O_C)+r\binom{m}{2}.$$
Consequently, for the normalization defect
$\delta_k$ of [[def-normalization-defect-of-reduced-curve]],
$$\delta_k(C')=\delta_k(C)-r\binom{m}{2}.$$

changes.before: For rank r=1, the unit is a basis of D by the local rank-one algebra argument. A chosen basis b_1=u·1 has u invertible, so its trace discriminant is u^2, a unit; it is 1 for the unit basis.
changes.after: The rank-one instance of the Statement and step 1.1 uses the trace matrix on the specified basis: locally the unit of a rank-one algebra generates its residue fibre, hence is a basis by Nakayama. Consequently D=A, a chosen basis b_1=u times 1 has u invertible, and the discriminant is u^2, a unit. It equals 1 for the unit basis; scalar extension preserves this calculation as in step 1.1.

changes.before: For D=0, its unit is zero, the empty tensor sum satisfies the identities, and every unital D-bimodule is zero. All cochains and the contraction identity are then zero.
changes.after: The Statement and steps 1.1 and 2.1 allow D=0. Its unit is zero, so the empty tensor sum gives e=0 and multiplication(e)=1=0. A unital D-bimodule is then zero, hence every multilinear cochain is zero and delta h+h delta=id is the zero-map identity.

changes.before: The empty cover pulls back to the empty cover and has its unique morphism to every cover. It has a section only if the base is empty. For X empty both cover categories have their sole empty object.
changes.after: The Statement and step 2.1 include the empty cover: in its internal-Hom construction the function set from E empty to any F is a singleton, whereas from E nonempty to F empty it is empty. Thus the empty cover has its unique map to every cover, but it has a section only over empty X. If X is empty, both cover categories have just the empty object, so the asserted equivalence holds.

changes.math_check: Step 3.1 quantifies every connected finite étale cover under the library convention. The empty cover, treated in step 1.1, remains empty and connected after restriction; nonempty connected covers give the transitive finite actions for surjectivity.
